pr.title: Hold a pull request in draft while changes for it are built
pr.head: 394c15a32354f9d7c3bc4bb5efe99db3e1773f30

summary: Projector runs two loops over the operator's pull requests. The review loop reviews each head and, on a pull request the operator wrote, uses draft state as its verdict: a clean review marks the pull request ready, and a review with findings returns it to draft. The fix loop runs fix-pr to answer the review's findings.

A clean review can still list Suggestions, small improvements that never block. Before this change, fix-pr weighed them on a whim, and nothing kept the pull request from looking ready to merge while fix-pr or the owner built a change that no review had read.

1. fix-pr decides every suggestion. It implements one that is small and clearly right, and defers the rest with a one-line reason in its report.
  2. It holds the pull request while it builds. It marks the pull request draft and posts a hold comment: a list of the changes coming, ending in the marker <!-- projector-hold v=1 -->. It deletes the comment once the push that carries them succeeds.
  3. The review side respects the hold. While the pull request's author has a hold open, project review status and publish report a new sign-off, held, and keep the pull request a draft. The review watcher watch-prs.sh stops asking for re-reviews until the hold is lifted.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Hold comment: an issue comment by the pull request's author whose body carries <!-- projector-hold v=1 -->. A comment with the marker from anyone else holds nothing.
  • Sign-off: the rule publish applies after each review to set draft state: changes-requested, held, waiting, clean, or unreviewed.
  • RESPONDED: the review watcher's request to re-review an unchanged head because the author answered without pushing.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The Projector review of 394c15a requested changes with one finding: fix-pr marks the pull request draft before it posts the hold, so a watcher pass between the two steps still announces RESPONDED and the review loop re-reviews an unchanged head. The flag sits on skills/fix-pr/SKILL.md.

groups.title: The sign-off reads the hold
groups.kicker: How publish and status learn about a hold, and what they do with it
intro: The sign-off is the rule that decides a self-reviewed pull request's draft state after each review. It already had four outcomes. This group adds a fifth, held, which applies when no model requests changes and the pull request's author has a hold comment open.

holds lists those comments through the REST issue-comments API, reading every page and keeping only the author's. signoff ranks held below changes-requested and above waiting. publish keeps a held self-review a draft. On a cross-author review it posts a COMMENT rather than an APPROVE. status prints a line for each open hold, and its JSON gains a holds list.

files.note: Adds HOLD_MARKER, holds, the held branch in signoff, and the author argument that sign, status, and publish pass through.

checks.text: Only the pull request's author can hold it. The login comparison is case-insensitive here, while the watcher compares GitHub's canonical logins exactly.

A held head maps to draft on a self-review and skips the peer wait, because only a draft about to be marked ready waits for peers. test_the_authors_hold_keeps_a_clean_head_a_draft_without_waiting_for_peers covers both starting states, and the full suite passed (763 tests).

files.note: Tests for held sign-off, a stranger's hold, change requests outranking a hold, cross-author approval, and status output. One test checks that fix-pr, the code, and the watcher agree on the comment's first line and marker.

groups.title: The review watcher waits out a hold
groups.kicker: watch-prs.sh stops asking for re-reviews while a hold is open
intro: watch-prs.sh polls each tracked pull request and prints one line per event. RESPONDED asks for a re-review of an unchanged head, and it fires when a draft has every thread resolved. Before this change, drafting a signed-off pull request was enough to trigger it. The re-review then found the unchanged head clean and marked the pull request ready again.

The GraphQL query now also reads the author and the newest 100 comments, and the row gains a held field. While a hold is open, the watcher records held in its state and announces nothing. When the hold is lifted on a draft, it prints RESPONDED … now that its hold is lifted once, because a review of that head may have run while the hold kept it a draft.

files.note: Adds the author, the comments, and the held field to the query, and the held branch ahead of the RESPONDED test.

checks.text: With the row flag at -, as it is after a clean review marks the pull request ready, a draft without a hold comment prints RESPONDED, and the same draft with the author's hold prints nothing. I checked both by running the watcher through the test suite's fake gh.

files.note: Covers a hold on an unchanged head, a hold seen together with a new head, and a stranger's marker.

groups.title: fix-pr decides suggestions and holds while it builds
groups.kicker: The fix side: what fix-pr implements, and how it posts and lifts the hold
intro: fix-pr answers one pull request's review work. It now treats every suggestion in the newest Projector review of the head, by each model, as a decision to make. It implements a suggestion that is small and clearly right, and defers the rest. An instruction from the owner overrides that default either way.

Before fix-pr builds a suggestion it implements, or a change the owner asks for, it holds the pull request. It marks it draft and posts the hold comment with gh api … -F body=@<file>, then reads the comment back to confirm the marker landed. It edits the same comment as more changes come in, and deletes it once the push that carries every change succeeds. It never marks the pull request ready itself; the review of the pushed head does that.

files.note: New sections Decide each suggestion and Hold the pull request while changes are built, plus the hold in the outstanding-work list, the clean conditions, and the report.

checks.text: Step 1 marks the pull request draft before step 2 posts the hold. A watcher pass between the two sees a draft with no hold and announces RESPONDED, so the review loop re-reviews an unchanged head. The review's finding asks to post the hold first. The comment alone already silences the watcher and keeps publish from marking the pull request ready.

files.note: Treats a review with Suggestions as work, routes an owner's change to the pull request's subagent, and reports a held pull request or stack layer as not ready.
